items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Trumpets were Jimmy Maxwell, Joe Newman, Joe Wilder and Johnny Frosk. ... Trombone were Jimmy Knepper, Willie Dennis and myself.

ctx.x: It was Zoot Sims, Tommy Newsom, I think Gene Allen was playing baritone, Phil Woods and Jerry Dodgion was playing second alto. Trombone were Jimmy Knepper, Willie Dennis and myself. Trumpets were Jimmy Maxwell, Joe Newman, Joe Wilder and Johnny Frosk. And the rhythm section was Mel Lewis, bass was Bill Crow and the piano was John Bunch. And the other piano player, who unfortunately didn’t get to play very much, Teddy Wilson. Can you believe that? He didn’t get to play. Benny wouldn’t let him play you know. After…
Oh yeah, Joya Sherrill. Well does he live up to his reputation? Did he live up to his reputation on that trip?

items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: We get to the hotel and Phil and Wayne get into an argument... So I picked Phil Woods over my shoulder... everyone's wondering, where is Zoot.

ctx.x: Wayne Andre, they're both hitting on this girl. She's sitting on my lap and there's some Georgian, I think he's a little sweet, was trying to hit on me, and it was a real complicated situation. She's sitting on my lap because there's no other room for her to sit. And David was sitting next to me.

We get to the hotel and Phil and Wayne get into an argument and Phil starts with the 'motherfucker.' And Wayne says, 'Just a minute, you son of a bitch, you can't speak like this in front of a fucking lady,' or something. In front of the Russian girl, you know. And these girls are pretty tough, they say they're KGB or whatever, you know. They're not shocked by anything. And they're going to square off and have a fight.
